rationale: Author-of-record walk of plan §Bead 7 against git show 694b9d46. The four plan steps are delivered faithfully and ONLY them: (1) guard.go gains entangleableClaimPaths (empty), EntangleableClaimPaths(), SetEntangleableClaimPathsForTest, CheckDirtyTreeProportional, IgnoredDirtNotice — 101 pure insertions, so CheckDirtyTree/CheckDirtyTreeDetail and DirtyTreeFailure are byte-identical by construction; release.go and internal/release are untouched (not in the commit at all). next.go Step 1 swaps to the proportional guard: blockingDirt still returns next.DirtyTreeFailure(cwd, blockingDirt, guard.ActiveWorktreePath(root)) — the identical call shape over the identical unchanged function, so the refusal-leg message contract is preserved byte-for-byte; ignoredDirt prints the one-line notice to stderr and proceeds with no exit-code change. The guard sits after the emit-only early return, so the notice fires only on the worktree-creating claim path, exactly matching the ADR fence. (2) spec.go extracts backfillExistingEpicPhase: absent-only backfill under bead-1's WithPhaseWriteLock (fn returns nil,nil for both no-op legs — phaselock.go's documented no-write contract), three distinct output messages (backfill / same-value nothing-mutated / later-phase-untouched), specMergeMetadataFn seam matching the plan*/impl*/adopt* convention; the plan's explicitly-not-taken fail-closed alternative is indeed not taken and the spec.go:73-74 existing-epic idempotence warning path is unchanged. I verified internal/phase's AC-5(vi) AST writer-inventory test still passes against the relocated call shape (go test ./internal/phase 18.7s ok). (3) The ADR-0025 amendment is present, MANDATORY per round-2 G3, and carries an explicit binding scope fence naming spec approve's tree-clean check and release's guard as keeping the unqualified sentence — scope-fenced to next's worktree-creating claim path only. (4) AC-8: three real bd+git e2e variants matching the three named dirt shapes (untracked file / untracked dir tree / modified tracked AGENTS.md), the enumeration pin derives a REAL claim run's porcelain diff (clean-before sanity + bidirectional match via length + membership), and AC-8(iii)'s seam-injected refusal leg drives assertDirtyTreeFailureInvariants over the blocking subset while asserting the merely-ignored path is NOT named in the failure. AC-16: all five legs present (empty-phase backfill with exactly one write of plan; same-value plan zero-write no-op that never claims a backfill; implement/review/done zero-write untouched legs naming the stored value) and they are red-on-revert (an unconditional write makes calls!=0 fail). I confirmed phase.Cache.AllEpics includes closed epics, so the closed-out-epic replay genuinely reaches this path and the done leg is the operative pin. next_dirty_test.go's rewrite is the necessary consequence of removing the block — the old test pinned the REMOVED behavior — and it keeps the M6 legacy-block regression pin and adds a binary-level stderr assertion that the notice names the dirt. I re-ran everything myself in the bead worktree: go build ok; internal/next 13.7s ok; internal/approve 50.8s ok; internal/phase 18.7s ok; the three cmd e2e tests PASS (337s, exit 0). Worktree left byte-identical (git status clean). ONE gap against the operator directive as recorded in bd key spec-128-bead7-warning-note: the directive requires the one-line diagnostic 'pinned by test per the spec's message discipline', and the spec's message discipline pins identifying text by substring (R6.3's pinned bypass line 'emit-only: bead fetched by ID; readiness not checked'; R3.1's golden baseline; assertDirtyTreeFailureInvariants). No test anywhere pins the notice's identifying wording — grep for 'claiming despite' / 'not blocked' across *_test.go finds nothing. Tests pin one-line-ness, per-path naming, escaping, and stderr routing, but the notice could be silently reworded (e.g. into something reading as an error, or dropping the 'not blocked — ADR-0025 R5.1' clause that makes it informational) with every test staying green. That is the one directive clause not fully delivered; the fix is two assertions.
concrete_changes_required: Pin the ignored-dirt notice's identifying wording per the spec's message discipline (operator directive, bd key spec-128-bead7-warning-note: 'one-line diagnostic, pinned by test'): in internal/next/entangle_test.go TestIgnoredDirtNotice_NamesEveryPathOnOneLine, assert the message contains the stable identifying substring(s) — 'claiming despite unrelated dirty path(s)' and 'not blocked — ADR-0025 R5.1' — and in cmd/mindspec/next_dirty_test.go strengthen the stderr assertion from Contains(stderr, "notes.txt") to also require the notice prefix, so a silent rewording (or replacement with a bare path dump / an error-shaped message) goes red at both the unit and real-binary levels.

findings.title: Notice wording unpinned — directive's 'pinned by test per the spec's message discipline' clause only partially delivered
findings.detail: IgnoredDirtNotice's tests pin one-line-ness, per-path naming, hostile-path escaping, and (via next_dirty_test.go) stderr routing in a real binary run, but no test asserts the notice's identifying text. grep -rn 'claiming despite|not blocked' over *_test.go returns nothing. The spec's message discipline elsewhere pins exact identifying substrings; the recorded operator directive invokes that discipline for this notice. A future edit could reword the line into an error-shaped or blame-shaped message — defeating the 'informational, visibility without the block' intent — with the whole suite green.

findings.title: Everything else verified faithful
findings.detail: Four plan steps delivered and only them (8 files, all in scope; the next_dirty_test.go rewrite is forced by the removed block and keeps the M6 pin). DirtyTreeFailure byte-identical (guard.go is 101 pure insertions; call shape unchanged). ADR-0025 amendment mandatory + explicitly scope-fenced to next's worktree-creating claim path, naming spec-approve and release as unaffected. Backfill's no-op legs use WithPhaseWriteLock's documented nil,nil no-write contract; AC-5(vi) writer-inventory AST test still green over the relocated seam. Emit-only branches off before the guard, so the notice cannot fire on non-claim paths. All suites re-run by this reviewer in the bead worktree: build + internal/next + internal/approve + internal/phase + the three cmd e2e tests all PASS; worktree left byte-identical.
